controlling_authority.section_title: 247 CMR 9.15: Verifying a Practitioner's Prescriptive Authority
controlling_authority.chapter_title: 247 CMR 9.00: Code for Professional Conduct; Professional Standards for Registered Pharmacists, Pharmacies, and Pharmacy Departments
controlling_authority.promulgating_body: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy
controlling_authority.verbatim_operative_text: (2) A pharmacist may not fill a prescription unless the pharmacist, in the exercise of his or her professional judgment, determines that: (a) the prescription was issued for a legitimate medical purpose by a practitioner acting in the usual course of his or her professional practice; (b) there is a valid patient-practitioner relationship; (c) the prescription is authentic; and (d) the dispensing is in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19(a).
controlling_authority.verbatim_adjacent_subsection_1: (1) A pharmacist who dispenses medications reported to the Massachusetts Prescription Monitoring Program (PMP) shall register with and maintain login information for the electronic system to monitor the prescribing and dispensing of controlled substances authorized by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A, known as PMP or MassPAT.

questions.independent_reasoning: The stem asks which determinations the regulation requires a pharmacist to make, in the exercise of professional judgment, before any prescription may be filled. The controlling Massachusetts provision is 247 CMR 9.15(2), which is a closed, enumerated list of four determinations gating the act of filling. It is not limited to controlled substances: the operative words are 'may not fill a prescription', which matches the stem's 'before any prescription may be filled'. Mapping the offered propositions onto the enumerated list: choice B reproduces 9.15(2)(a) essentially verbatim (legitimate medical purpose by a practitioner acting in the usual course of professional practice); choice C reproduces 9.15(2)(b) verbatim (valid patient-practitioner relationship); choice E reproduces 9.15(2)(c) verbatim (the prescription is authentic). Those three are therefore required determinations. The fourth enumerated determination, 9.15(2)(d) (dispensing in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19(a)), is not offered as a choice, which is permissible in a select-all-that-apply item and does not affect the correctness of B, C and E. Choice A fails because no Massachusetts Controlled Substances Registration determination appears anywhere in the enumerated list; a full-text scan of the official 247 CMR 9.00 document returned zero occurrences of 'MCSR' or 'Controlled Substances Registration'. Prescriber registration is governed elsewhere and is not one of the professional-judgment determinations 9.15(2) imposes as a precondition to filling. Choice D fails because the PMP obligation that 247 CMR 9.15 places on the pharmacist is in subsection (1) and is a registration and login-maintenance duty, not a determination inside the 9.15(2) list; 9.15(2) contains no PMP screening element. Both A and D are drawn from the immediate regulatory neighbourhood of the correct rule, which is why they are attractive, but neither is a member of the enumerated set the stem asks about.

per_choice_blind_analysis.basis: Not among the determinations enumerated in 247 CMR 9.15(2). Full-text search of the official 247 CMR 9.00 document found no occurrence of 'MCSR' or 'Controlled Substances Registration'.
247 CMR 9.15(1) imposes a PMP registration and login-maintenance duty on the pharmacist. It is not one of the professional-judgment determinations enumerated in 247 CMR 9.15(2).

candidate_alternative_readings_tested: Whether 247 CMR 9.01 (professional conduct standards) supplies a competing or broader list of pre-fill determinations. Rejected: the other occurrences of 'professional judgment' in the official document concern generic substitution and patient counselling, not preconditions to filling.

Whether 9.15(2) is confined to controlled substances because of the section heading and the PMP subject matter of 9.15(1). Rejected: 9.15(2) says 'a prescription' without limitation, and (2)(d) separately cross-references M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19(a) rather than restricting scope.
Whether subsection (1)'s PMP duty could be read into the (2) list. Rejected: (1) and (2) are structurally distinct, and (2) is introduced by its own closed 'determines that:' enumeration.
second_reasonable_legal_reading_consider.conclusion: No second reasonable legal reading survives. 247 CMR 9.15(2) is a closed enumerated list and the mapping of B, C and E onto (a), (b) and (c) is exact.

questions.confidence_basis: Choices B, C and E track the official regulatory text essentially word for word, and the two rejected propositions are provably absent from the enumerated list by full-text search of the official document.
